## Question 1 (Assignment)

a) Why is it important to give your objects in R good names? {{< hp glyph="." >}}When might poorly thought-out names cause problems for a programmer?

b) Help me fix my code! "I want to calculate the average of three objects corresponding to negative emotion self-reports."


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
anger <- 3
sadness <- 4
fear <- 3
negative_emotion <- (anger + sadness + faer) / 3
## Error:
## ! object 'faer' not found
```
:::


## Question 2 (Functions)

a) In your own words, explain what functions and arguments are (in the context of programming) {{< hp glyph="." >}}and why they are useful in data science. 

b) Use nested functions and operations to achieve all of the following in a **single** line of code: multiply 45 by 3.14, then divide the result by 180, then calculate that value's sine, and then round the result to the nearest even integer.

## Question 3 (Arguments)

a) In your own words, explain what a "default value" is for an argument {{< hp glyph="." >}}and why it might be important for the people who create functions to choose those default values carefully.

b) Help me fix my code! "I want to round 1/16 to three decimal places."


::: {.cell renv.ignore='true'}

```{.r .cell-code}

```
:::

## Question 5 (Strings)

a) Save the country names from the table in Question 4 to a character vector called `country`. {{< hp glyph="." >}}Calculate the number of characters in each country name and print that.

b) Use a function in R to calculate the average number of characters in each country name (i.e., use the function I taught you in class).


## Question 6 (Packages)
